_comment: Team Tether rank palettes (spec sec36), on top of NP1's palette and accessory mechanisms. CLAUDE.md/D24: human NPCs reuse an installed rig, never a new mesh. NP2-grunt-wire: grunt/officer/captain now build on `assets/characters/grunt/grunt_lod0.glb` (wired into art.json's `grunt` key by this same item) rather than the Warden's own rig -- a blind visual pass rejected the old ladder outright ('the four antagonist rank frames are not four characters, they are the Warden's exact mesh, costume and pose four times'), and the SAME critique named the second cost of that shortcut: reusing the boss's own body for his subordinates makes the boss stop being unique the moment the player has already fought three 'captains' wearing his face. The Warden keeps his own rig below -- he is the only rank with no `base` override -- specifically so meeting him still reads as meeting someone new.
_comment_single_material: All of today's human rigs, the grunt included (confirmed directly against the imported .glb: one MeshInstance3D, one surface, one 'Material_1'), carry exactly one fused material (character_model.gd's own _apply_palette comment), and that material's emission channel (a full-white self-lit copy of the same painted texture, fixed alongside this item so palette tints are visible at all -- see character_model.gd's _shared_variant_material) means a body-only palette can shift how BRIGHT the same outfit reads, never a genuinely different colour family. A first pass using body brightness alone (grunt darkest, warden full original) did not survive blind review: it read as a lighting gradient, not a rank system -- 'someone duplicated a mesh four times and nudged an exposure value.'
_comment_badge: So the real rank marker is a chest badge (NP1's existing 'accessories' mechanism -- a placeholder primitive on its own material, independent of the body palette, per CLAUDE.md's Prototyping section) that escalates in colour, size, SHAPE and FINISH. The shape ladder is stud, bigger stud, medal, larger polished medal: grunt and officer are spheres, captain and the Warden are `disc`s. It got there in two corrections, both from blind rounds. First, officer and captain were both spheres differing by '26 points in one colour channel and nothing else... a debug gizmo left in the shot', so captain took a different silhouette. The box chosen then was the wrong one and the next round photographed why: a cube shows ONE flat face to the camera, a plane takes a single shade under a single key, and the accessory material was matte by default -- so the captain's insignia rendered as a flat pure-red untextured rectangle with no gradient on it anywhere. A `CapsuleMesh` was tried for officer earlier and rejected for a different reason: `_primitive_mesh`'s own proportions (height = 2x size) render it as a ~20cm vertical pill at officer's badge size -- a bandolier, not a badge. See `captain._comment_badge_shape` for what the disc, the metal and the size drop each fix, and `_comment_badge_finish` for why the shading model mattered more than either the shape or the palette did.
_comment_oxblood: The same pass named a faction-identity gap on top of the rank-ladder one: 'the Warden and his ranks wear dark green and gold -- the same olive-green family as Grandpa's vest and the villager female's jacket... nothing on any antagonist costume carries the oxblood accent that would tie them to the stronghold's banners.' `data/config/palette.json`'s own `_reserved` comment says `tether_oxblood` (#332228) is meant for exactly this: 'Team Tether banners, equipment AND UNIFORMS, never on friendly or neutral elements.' Grunt/officer/captain's body palette below is a warm rose-red family multiplied onto the grunt rig's own dark tactical texture (never onto a friendly rig -- the reserved colour stays off Grandpa, the trainer and every villager, all of which keep their own established tints untouched), and every badge below sits in that same warm-red family rather than orange, with the Warden's own badge set to the literal reserved hex -- the one place in the ladder where the exact stronghold-banner colour appears, at the top of the same chain of command it marks.
_comment_badge_offset: NP2-grunt-wire also fixes the floating badge itself. The OLD offset ([0, 0.30, 0.25] from the Spine02 bone) was authored with no measurement behind it and put the sphere roughly 60% of the way from Spine02 to the Head bone -- near the throat/collar, not the chest -- and 0.25m forward of a bone whose own body surface sits at roughly 0.14-0.16m forward at THAT height once the actual mesh is sampled: the sphere's near edge alone cleared the coat, so the whole badge hung in open air in front of it ('reads as a debug gizmo left in the shot... it visibly hovers detached'). Every offset below was derived by building each rig headless (no render needed -- `_shared/render_bounds.gd`'s own fit maths plus a raw vertex sample of the body mesh near the target height, both plain CPU geometry) and reading the ACTUAL bone position and chest depth off it, not assumed: `y=0.10` sits roughly a fifth of the way from Spine02 to Head on both rigs (upper chest, well short of the collar), and each `z` is that rig's own measured chest-forward extent at that height, pulled back by roughly 60% of the badge's own radius so a sphere sits mostly EMBEDDED in the coat with only its own front third or so proud of the surface -- a worn pin, not a hovering ball. VIS-CAST re-derived every `z` below rather than carrying the old numbers forward, because the badges got SMALLER and a smaller badge pulled back by the old amount sinks out of sight: the two chest depths those offsets encode (~0.140m on the grunt rig, ~0.158m on the Warden's) are recovered from the measurements above and re-applied to the new radii. The two `disc` badges are thin rather than round, so they take no 60% pull-back at all -- a medal is worn ON a coat, and its centre sits at the coat's own surface with half its ~2cm thickness proud. Bigger badges (captain, warden) therefore show a slightly bigger visible bump than grunt's, which is the intended reading: the badge gets both larger and more physically present as rank rises.
_comment_badge_finish: VIS-CAST: `metallic`/`metallic_specular`/`roughness` are optional per-accessory keys read by character_model.gd's `_shared_variant_material`. They exist because the default accessory material is matte (roughness 1.0, metallic 0.0), which on a flat-faced primitive under one directional key renders as a single uniform colour -- the shading model, not the shape or the palette, is what made the rank badges read as debug gizmos in two consecutive blind rounds. Metal rises with rank alongside size and colour, so the ladder escalates in finish as well: a grunt's stud is dull, the Warden's medal is polished.

grunt.label: Grunt
grunt._comment_palette: Dark oxblood, the lowest value of the three ranks. These three hexes were desaturated pinks (#a27d7d/#bb9090/#d4a3a3) for as long as the emission floor was a MULTIPLY, because a dark tint crushed both channels toward black and the only defence was to keep luminance high. The floor is additive now, which removes that constraint completely -- a dark, saturated tint is guaranteed a visible floor regardless of how dark the texel under it is -- so the palette can be the reserved colour instead of a pale relative of it. A blind round measured the previous pass at saturation 0.20-0.24 and value 0.25-0.31 against the UNRANKED archetype's 0.19, and named the consequence exactly: applying a rank made the uniform LIGHTER and greyer than standard issue, so 'the standard issue body looks more elite than every rank above it'. Ranks now sit at or below the archetype in value and well above it in saturation, which is the right direction for a uniform.
grunt._comment_palette_crush: STRANDED-P3, confirmed game bug (kept for the mechanism, not the old hex -- see character_model.gd's `_shared_variant_material` for the actual fix): a straight albedo*colour multiply can only ever DARKEN a source pixel, and this rig's shared material also copies the same rank colour into the self-lit emission channel, so a dark tint crushes both channels toward black at once. character_model.gd's ADDITIVE emission floor (lerp toward the tint colour whenever tint luminance < 0.95) is what actually keeps a dark uniform legible; this hex is chosen with headroom above that floor's comfortable range on top, not as a substitute for it.

officer.label: Officer
officer._comment_palette: Same oxblood family, one value step up -- the secondary cue underneath the badge's own shape/colour/size change. See grunt's note for why these three moved off pale pink.

captain.label: Captain
captain._comment_palette: Brightest of the three grunt-rig ranks and the top of the value ladder, still darker and far more saturated than the unranked archetype. See grunt's note.
captain._comment_badge_shape: VIS-CAST. The box this replaces was itself a fix -- 'officer and captain differ by 26 points in one colour channel and nothing else' -- and it solved that and introduced a worse defect the next blind round photographed: a 13cm cube presents ONE flat face square to the camera, a plane takes exactly one shade across the whole of it under a single key, and the accessory material was a default StandardMaterial3D at roughness 1.0 with no metal, so the result had no gradient anywhere on it. It rendered as a flat pure-red untextured rectangle pasted over the chest straps -- a debug gizmo again, in a new shape. Three things change together, because none of them is sufficient alone: the shape becomes a `disc` (a struck medal, whose rim curves away from the key so the silhouette is lit on one edge and shaded on the other), the material gets real metal (character_model.gd's `finish` block) so the face carries a specular falloff instead of one flat value, and the size drops from 0.13 to 0.095 -- 13cm is a placard, not insignia. The colour also comes off full saturation, because a pure hue chip is the other half of why it read as UI rather than as an object on a costume. The rank ladder is unchanged in kind: stud, bigger stud, medal, and the Warden's larger polished medal in the literal reserved hex.

warden.label: Warden
warden._comment: No `base` key -- the only rank that does NOT reuse the grunt rig, and no palette override either: his own board-16 painted finish (D49's rebuild) is the reference-authored look and stays untouched, the same call this file made before NP2-grunt-wire. Sphere again rather than a fourth new shape, back at the top of the same size ladder (largest, 0.16) the other three climb -- the thing that makes him unmistakably the top of the chain is now his OWN body, not a bigger gizmo.
warden._comment_oxblood_top: The one badge that carries the literal `tether_oxblood` hex (#332228) rather than a warm-red relative of it -- the Warden sits at the top of the same faction the reserved colour belongs to, so his own insignia is where the exact stronghold-banner colour actually appears, and everything below him is visibly in that colour's family without repeating it exactly. VIS-CAST keeps the hex and fixes what it cost: #332228 is near-black, his board-16 coat is dark green, and a matte near-black sphere on dark cloth is invisible at any distance a player meets him from. It is now a POLISHED disc (metallic 0.88, roughness 0.16) -- a specular highlight reads against dark cloth even when the base colour does not, so the reserved colour stays exactly the reserved colour and the insignia is still findable. The alternative, brightening the hex, would have spent the one place in the game where the banner colour appears literally.

_comment_scale: Every human rig (trainer/Grandpa/Warden/grunt) sits under an Armature node with a flat 0.01 scale -- HANDOFF.md sec6's 'centimetre-unit skeleton under a 0.01 Armature node with x100 inverse binds', the same bug that produced the giant-player fit issue. character_model.gd's _attach_part() sets a placeholder's `position` as a LOCAL child of a BoneAttachment3D inside that scaled chain, so both `offset` and `size` below are in that same shrunk local space, not real metres: a size of 13.0 here renders as a 0.13m sphere in the actual game world, and an offset of 30 along one axis moves it 0.30m in world space. Measured directly (offset [30,0,0]/[0,30,0]/[0,0,30] each moved the attached part almost exactly 0.30m along the matching WORLD axis with no rotation to account for), not guessed -- confirmed the shared _attach_part() mechanism NP1's hair also uses has this same scale, so hair's own tiny offset (0.08) is likely rendering at ~0.0008m, effectively invisible too. Left untouched here rather than fixed for everyone: changing hair's placement is a real, currently-unverified visual change outside NP2's scope, not a call to make inside this item.
_comment_badge_scale: Badge sizes and offsets are METRES -- character_model.gd's own default (`acc.get("size", 0.12)`) is the giveaway: 12cm is what a chest badge should be. The values above are already in that space; see `_comment_badge_offset` above for how the current `offset` numbers were actually derived (measured per rig, not guessed) and what defect that fixes.
